bullets.title: Fed hike risk rising: Core PCE tracking well above Fed's threshold
bullets.body: Nine FOMC participants now favor hikes as baseline; only one favors cuts. Core PCE needs to print ~0.21% monthly to match the Fed's revised 3.3% 2026 forecast, but recent readings are tracking ~0.36% — well above the threshold. Markets are pricing zero cuts in 2026 at 80%, with a 52% probability of at least one hike this year (up 2pp w/w), and July hike odds rose to 20% (up 14pp w/w).

bullets.title: S&P +0.9% to 7,483; semis rip on Trump-Intel/Apple chip comments
bullets.body: SOXX ETF surged 4.38% as Trump announced Apple has agreed to work with Intel to build chips in America. INTC gained 8-10% in pre-market; broad semiconductor sector strength across foundries, equipment, and memory names (MU, WDC, STX, AVGO, AMD). VIX rose 7.5% to 17.06, consistent with a risk-on tape with some hedging activity.

bullets.title: FERC unanimously approves Trump plan to fast-track AI data center grid connections
bullets.body: FERC voted unanimously to direct grid operators to allow large loads — including AI data centers — to connect in a 'timely and orderly manner,' removing a key infrastructure bottleneck for AI build-out. The ruling is broadly positive for power and data center infrastructure plays.

bullets.title: ACN -17%: Bookings miss and guidance cut fuel AI services bear case
bullets.body: Accenture F3Q revenue of $18.72B missed consensus by 0.3%; bookings of $19.3B fell 2% YoY vs. +7% consensus, with Managed Services book-to-bill falling below 1.0x for the first time since 2019. FY26 revenue growth guidance was cut to 3-4% from 3-5%, and Morgan Stanley sees the miss as a negative read-across for European IT services. The miss is amplifying the AI-cannibalization narrative for software/services: ACN is down ~42% YTD despite being positioned as a leading AI consulting beneficiary.

bullets.title: Macro data solid: Philly Fed back in expansion, claims subdued, capex plans at post-COVID highs
bullets.body: June Philly Fed manufacturing PMI rose to 10.3 (ISM-adjusted 53.1, up from 49.7), with new orders and shipments driving expansion; capex plans hit post-COVID highs supported by instant-expensing provisions. Initial claims fell 4k w/w to 226k; JPMorgan's 2Q26 global capex nowcast rose to 10.4% SAAR from 6.8% in 1Q, with investment goods PMI at 54.4 vs. 51.8. Prices paid rose while prices received declined, flagging margin pressure.

bullets.title: GOOGL renting GPUs at $50/watt — signals AI compute scarcity and high monetization bar
bullets.body: Google is reportedly renting ~110K NVIDIA GB300 GPUs at ~$50/watt annually, a rate materially above the ~$12-14/watt typical neocloud contract rate. MS raises AI capex estimates for GOOGL to $375B ('28), AMZN to $244B, META to $205B. The deal is seen as bullish for hyperscaler AI monetization but raises the bar for ROI across the entire AI infrastructure stack.

bullets.title: AAPL calling memory costs a 'hundred-year flood'; iPhone price hikes unavoidable
bullets.body: Apple's CEO cited memory costs as a crisis, with DRAM/NAND BOM costs rising 80-90% YTD and triple digits YoY. Memory as a share of smartphone/PC BOM is moving from mid-teens to 25-30%. AAPL is planning to raise iPhone 18 and Mac/iPad prices by $100-200+ ASP; hyperscalers pre-paying and locking long-term memory supply are pushing AAPL to the back of the queue.

bullets.title: AI traffic data: Ramp spend up 15x since Jan 2025; AI-sourced retail visits convert 54% better
bullets.body: Ramp data shows AI spend up 15x since January 2025, with token spend per business up 14% m/m; DeepSeek remains tiny at 0.4% of Ramp firms. Adobe data shows AI-sourced traffic to US retail rose 138% YoY in May 2026, up 1,324% since October 2024; AI-referred shoppers convert 54% better, stay 53% longer, and browse 23% more pages. Adobe also showed AI-driven travel traffic up 194% in May.

bullets.title: 800V DC power architecture emerging as gating factor for AI factory scaling
bullets.body: Citi and others flag 800V DC data center power as a critical infrastructure transition starting 2027, reducing current by ~15x vs. 54V systems and enabling multi-megawatt racks. TXN is seen as best positioned due to high-voltage GaN and 300mm capacity; TAM estimated to grow 75% CAGR from $2B (2025) to $12B (2028). NVIDIA's Vera Rubin NVL72 delivers 10x more tokens/megawatt vs. GB200 and sets 800V as the next-gen standard.

bullets.title: WFE estimates lifted to $145B/'26, $200B/'27, $250B/'28 on hyperscaler capex acceleration
bullets.body: Citi raises wafer fab equipment forecasts materially on accelerating hyperscaler capex, with capital goods industrial production for 2Q26 tracking at 12.7% vs. 5.5% in 1Q26. AMAT PT raised to $710, LRCX to $450, KLAC to $290. Emerging markets capex nowcast rose to 21.5% for 2Q26 vs. 18.6% in 1Q.

bullets.title: AMZN exploring selling custom AI chips to third parties as NVDA alternative
bullets.body: Amazon is in discussions to sell its custom AI chips for data center use to other companies, according to Bloomberg, positioning its silicon as a lower-cost inference alternative to NVIDIA. This dovetails with UBS noting Microsoft is moving Copilot to usage-based pricing and considering cheaper DeepSeek alternatives, pointing to a broader rotation from AI 'spenders' (hyperscalers) toward 'receivers' (memory, optical, HDD).

bullets.title: BoE holds with hawkish dissent; JPM pushes first hike to November
bullets.body: The Bank of England held rates 7-2, with Greene and Pill dissenting in favor of a 25bp hike. JPMorgan pushed back its first-hike call from July to November, but Bailey flagged risks to inflation and rates are to the upside. PMI pricing data suggests limited second-round effects have emerged so far, though the BoE risks acting only after they clearly materialize.

bullets.title: Prediction markets: Oil downside risk spikes on Iran peace deal; US recession odds at 13%
bullets.body: WTI below $65 in 2026 priced at 43% (up 15pp w/w) as US-Iran diplomatic progress accelerated: US/Iran meeting by June 30 at 85% (up 53pp w/w), Strait of Hormuz normalization by July 31 at 56% (up 32pp w/w). US recession by year-end 2026 sits at just 13% (down 6pp w/w), while zero Fed cuts in 2026 stands at 80%.

bullets.title: IBM CEO warns planned 125GW AI data center capacity could require $8-12T and disappoint
bullets.body: IBM CEO Arvind Krishna argues current AI deployments use oversized models for simple tasks and foundation models are becoming commodities. He flagged that planned 125GW of AI data center capacity could require $8T-$12T cumulative spending, with some investments disappointing as supply outpaces demand — a notable cautionary note amid aggressive hyperscaler capex build-out narratives.

bullets.title: Software sector under pressure: ACN whiff reinforces AI cannibalization; Tech Services sector leads 52-week lows
bullets.body: Software sector is down 17% in June alone after a 44% rally, and the Technology Services sector leads 52-week lows with 45 names. ACN's miss reinforces concerns that AI is cannibalizing traditional IT services revenue. Notable YTD decliners include ACN -58%, INTU -65%, ADBE -49%, CRM broadly lower — while hardware/memory (INTC +529%, MU +821%, WDC +1245% YoY) dominate the 52-week high list.

bullets.title: May retail sales accelerated to +6.9%; AI-sourced commerce traffic surging
bullets.body: US May retail sales rose 6.9% (ex-auto +7.5%), accelerating ~210bps sequentially with strength in sporting goods, electronics, and building materials; furniture and autos weak. AI-sourced retail visits surged 138% YoY in May and are up 1,324% since October 2024, with AI-referred shoppers converting 54% better than non-AI traffic.

bullets.title: META's China Manus acquisition blocked; Chinese backers plan to re-acquire at same $2B price
bullets.body: China's NDRC blocked Meta's acquisition of autonomous AI agent company Manus; Meta has been unwinding the deal, stopping data sharing and 'sunsetting' Manus. Manus's original Chinese backers (including Tencent, HSG, ZhenFund) are planning to re-acquire the company at the same $2B price paid in late December 2025.

bullets.title: Tariff pass-through fading but margin squeeze intensifying for consumer discretionary
bullets.body: Philadelphia Fed data shows prices received decelerating for a second consecutive month, suggesting tariff pass-through is ending — but prices paid accelerated, pinching margins. Oppenheimer warns broad tariff-driven price hikes remain a headwind to discretionary spending, with NKE, LULU, and FIGS facing significant unmitigated costs; preferred tariff-defense plays are AZO, CVNA, LTH, and W.

bullets.title: S&P 500 valuation only defensible if AI capex generates strong ROI — range-bound until Core PCE breaks
bullets.body: 22V notes S&P 500 valuations appear reasonable only if AI capex generates strong returns; cash return ratios have declined as tech prioritizes investment. Markets are likely range-bound until Core PCE breaks decisively lower; early cyclicals remain favored in a benign-slowdown scenario. Credit spread stability and household/corporate surplus conditions support the benign base case.

bullets.title: OpenAI poaches Noam Shazeer from Google; META exploring equity raise of tens of billions
bullets.body: OpenAI recruited Noam Shazeer — credited with 'fixing' Gemini 3 — from Google as research lead. META is separately exploring external capital structures including bond JVs, sovereign wealth partnerships, and potentially a multi-billion equity raise to fund its AI infrastructure build. Over 85 ex-Salesforce employees have moved to Anthropic and OpenAI in 2026, mostly in sales and marketing.
